applies_to: AERCO Benchmark E (BMK E) condensing boilers with the Edge X controller, including BST cascade plants; the table also lists the legacy Benchmark (BMK) Edge equivalents.
summary: The Edge X controller on AERCO's Benchmark E boilers talks BACnet IP on its Ethernet port or BACnet MS/TP on its RS-485 port. Standalone and client units expose their own setpoints and readings, while a BST cascade manager also exposes plant-level values and a block of read-only points for every unit in the cascade (up to 16). Only analog inputs (read only) and analog values (read/write) are used.
notes: A technician-level password is needed on the controller before BAS points are available.
BACnet vendor ID is 983; device profile B-ASC; ReadProperty and WriteProperty only, no segmentation.
Cascade unit points repeat in blocks: unit 1 uses IDs 300-320, unit 2 uses 400-420, and so on up to unit 16 at 1800-1820.
The manual lists one BAS connection per cascade manager or standalone unit; cascade members talk to the manager over Modbus RS-485.
Several IDs carry different names or ranges on legacy Benchmark (BMK) Edge units; legacy names are given in the descriptions, and points marked legacy BMK only are not used on BMK E.
Temperatures are listed in °F; AV 8 switches the BAS interface between English and Metric.

integration.summary: Enable the BAS port in the Edge X Comm & Failsafe menu (BACnet IP on the J5 Ethernet jack or MS/TP on the RS-485 terminals), choose the comm-loss behaviour, then have the BAS write the setpoint. For a cascade, connect the BAS to the BST manager only; it exposes plant values plus a read-only block for each unit. A technician-level password is needed before BAS points are available.

minimum_points.why: Selects constant, remote or outdoor-reset setpoint

minimum_points.name: Remote Signal
minimum_points.why: Set to BAS so the remote setpoint comes from BACnet

minimum_points.name: Setpoint

integration.enable: On the controller go to Settings > Advanced Setup > Comm & Failsafe and enable BAS; for IP turn on the "BAS (J6)" toggle, which actually uses the J5 jack. The object list has no separate start/stop object: the BAS controls the unit through AV 12 Operating Mode, AV 13 Remote Signal (0 = BAS) and the setpoint in AV 4, or AV 200 on a BST manager. Firing-rate control (Direct Drive) is listed only for legacy BMK units.
integration.heartbeat: The BAS Comm Failsafe setting chooses whether the unit shuts down or runs at a constant setpoint when it loses the BAS (AV 24 Unit Failsafe Mode: 0 = Standby, 1 = Constant Setpt). The BACnet IP screen also has a delay-before-communication-fault setting; its range and default are not given.
integration.remote_sensors: AV 85 / AV 213 Supply Header Temp Source and AV 215 return header source can be set to BAS (2), but the object list has no writable header or outdoor temperature value. On BMK E the outdoor sensor source (AV 81 / AV 217) is listed as Direct only.
setup: BACnet IP settings on the controller include DHCP on/off, IP address, a device-instance offset to avoid duplicates, the UDP port, network number and comm-fault delay; defaults are not printed.
MS/TP uses the same configuration screen with only the baud rate added; wire to J16 pins 5 (+) and 7 (-) on the I/O board and use the MODBUS1 (SW4) TERM1 switch at the ends of the BAS trunk.
One BAS connection per cascade manager or standalone unit; manager and clients talk to each other over Modbus RS-485.
BACnet vendor ID 983; ReadProperty and WriteProperty only, no segmentation.
gotchas: Cascade unit blocks: unit 1 = AI 300-320, unit 2 = AI 400-420 ... unit 16 = AI 1800-1820.
Several IDs have different names or ranges on legacy Benchmark (BMK) Edge units; check which controller you have.
AV 8 switches the BAS interface between English and Metric units.
